## When to use

Use a link when you need a web address: a practice's website, a profile page, a shared document. The form checks that the answer is a complete address before it can be sent.

Use something else when:

- **You need an email address.** Use Email.
- **The respondent may not know the full address.** Use Short answer and ask for a name instead, such as the practice's name.

## Add it in the builder

You need a form open in the editor.

1. Below the last block, select **+** (Insert a block), or type `/` in the line beside it.
2. Under **Questions**, choose **Link**. Typing `url` or `website` in the search box finds it too. The question is added and its settings open.
<Gif alt="Inserting a Link question from the block menu" />
3. In **Label**, write the question.
4. Add **Help text** saying the address must start with https://.
5. Turn on **Required** if the question must be answered.
6. Select **Save**.

## Settings

| Builder setting | Schema property | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Label | `label` | "Website / URL" |
| Help text | `description` | none; left out of the file when empty |
| Required | `required` | `false` |
| Name (only inside a group with a score) | not in the downloaded file | made from the label |
| Show this question only when… | `enableWhen`, and `enableLogic` with two or more conditions | none |

The box shows "https://…" until the respondent types. The builder has no setting to change that.

**As a condition.** Other questions can be shown depending on a link, with is answered, is or is not.

## Validation and error messages

The form checks the answer when the respondent selects Submit (or Next, on a form with pages). Each message shows under the question and in the "There is a problem" summary at the top of the form, where it links to the question. Once a message shows, it updates as the respondent types, and it goes when the answer is fixed.

| Situation | Message |
|---|---|
| Required, and nothing typed | "Referring practice's website" is required. (the question's own label, in quotation marks) |
| Required, and only spaces typed | The same message: an answer of only spaces counts as no answer. |
| The answer isn't a complete web address | Enter a valid URL, including https://. |

A complete address starts with its scheme, such as `https://`. An address such as example.org, without it, is refused. The check ignores spaces before or after the address, and doesn't check that the address exists.

## Accessibility

What the rendered form exposes to assistive technology:

- The question is a native URL input (`type="url"`), named by its label.
- Help text, then any error, are linked to the input as its description (`aria-describedby`).
- A required question has the native `required` attribute. The red asterisk is hidden from assistive technology, so it is never read out as part of the name.
- After a failed check, the input has `aria-invalid="true"`.

| Check | Status |
|---|---|
| Automated: axe, WCAG 2.2 A and AA | No violations on the live example above, in light and dark, with and without its error shown. Checked by the docs' own tests. |
| Contrast | Covered by axe's contrast rule in the same tests: the renderer's default colours, light and dark. |
| Screen reader | [TODO: not tested with a screen reader yet.] |

## Troubleshooting

**"Enter a valid URL, including https://." for an address that looks right.** The address has no scheme, as in example.org. The form doesn't add `https://` for the respondent, so ask for it in the help text.

**An answer that isn't a website was accepted.** The check accepts any complete address, whatever its scheme, so `mailto:` and `tel:` addresses pass too.
